answer: Bind each identity to one examined patent filing verified against a patent register. The applicant name must match the identity holder, the filing must have passed examination, and one filing backs one identity; a second identity citing the same filing, inventor, or assignee is merged and suspended. A hollow quartz sensor or a cedar preservative counts only once examined, not merely filed. A farm therefore needs a genuinely novel, examined invention per fake, paying drafting and examination fees and risking prior-art rejection, and one proven fraudulent filing revokes the whole cluster.
